decisions.reason: As a close-to-core software product that fits the firm's move toward connected and data-driven infrastructure management, it is likely to stay unless several years of sales and usage have clearly fallen below aspiration.

Because this software seems less prominently established than Product A and may overlap with other archiving/reporting offerings, management would be inclined to reallocate resources if its results have persistently lagged aspiration.

This more niche hardware item is less central to the firm's increasingly digital systems direction, so if its performance has remained uncertain the firm would use problemistic search and shift resources back to stronger core activities.

Control technology for water engineering machinery is highly complementary to the firm's established integrated systems business, making it likely to be retained with slack even if recent outcomes were somewhat noisy.

A web-prominent automation and system software product launched recently enough to justify continued learning is well aligned with the firm's strategic trajectory, so management would usually keep it unless there were clear signs of sustained underperformance.
